ai.title: Add example file retrieval to request-files-prompt
ai.summary: Introduces `generateExampleFilesPrompt` in `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts` to fetch example files alongside key files. Uses Haiku model to identify relevant code examples based on user/assistant prompts and project context, excluding `knowledge.md`. Results merged into `keyResults` via `Promise.all`. Error handling logs failures and returns empty arrays.

eli5.text: When you ask for help with code, the assistant can now also pull up relevant example files alongside the key files it already fetches, so you get worked examples that match what you're asking for. The examples are picked by a separate lightweight model and skip over your knowledge notes, and they're merged together with the key files in one response. If anything goes wrong while grabbing examples, it quietly skips them instead of failing your request, and you'd only notice if you were specifically looking at the backend source file that orchestrates the file retrieval.

ai.title: System prompt clarifies latest file version usage
ai.summary: System prompt updated to explicitly instruct model to use only the last copy of file. New `createMarkdownFileBlock` helper in `common/src/util/file.ts` formats content with triple backticks and path. This change targets `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to reduce confusion from multiple file versions in context.

eli5.text: The system that generates instructions for the coding assistant now explicitly tells it to treat the last version of any file as the correct one, rather than relying on the assistant to figure that out. When files are included in those instructions, they are now wrapped in a code-style block that labels each file by name, making it visually clear which copy is which. This is live today and affects anything you ask the assistant to edit when multiple versions of a file have been passed along in the same request.

ai.title: Tighten file-block rewrite prompt to force full file output
ai.summary: Rewrote the file-block processing prompt in backend/src/process-file-block.ts to explicitly require the full, complete file content, forbidding excerpts. This change aims to prevent lazy model responses that return partial code blocks during file rewrites. Scope is limited to the backend prompt construction logic. The prompt now adds 'Do not excerpt portions of the file, write out the entire updated file.' to the instruction set.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to update a file, the instruction now explicitly tells it to write out the entire file content instead of just describing the changes or returning partial content. This applies to the backend system that constructs prompts for file rewriting tasks. If you were watching, you would notice that the rewritten file is now more likely to include the full file content rather than excerpts. This change is live today.

ai.title: Rename Manicode to Codebuff in web app
ai.summary: Web application branding and internal references updated from Manicode to Codebuff. Changes span documentation (README, knowledge.md), UI components (navbar, footer, home page), and configuration constants. CLI installation instructions and external links (npm, Product Hunt, YC) now point to codebuff. Error message text simplified in referral helpers.

eli5.text: The software's name shown in the web app was changed from Manicode to Codebuff. You would notice this if you visited the website or read its help pages, where the logo and company name now say Codebuff instead of Manicode, and links to external sites like Product Hunt and Y Combinator point to Codebuff profiles. The instructions for installing and using the tool via the command line were also updated to use 'codebuff' instead of 'manicode'. This change affects anyone using the web app's interface, documentation, or referral system.

ai.title: Updated favicon assets
ai.summary: Replaced favicon.ico, favicon-16x16.ico, and apple-touch-icon.png with new logo assets. Updates affect web/public/favicon directory. No functional code changes.

eli5.text: The small icon that appears in your browser tab and on your phone's home screen when you bookmark the site has been swapped for a new version of the company logo. The picture changed, but nothing about how the site works did, and there are no new features or fixes to try out.
